notes:
Summary: Prism is an enterprise KM vendor (legal+consulting verticals) with a large RAG footprint. Focus: move from self-hosted SBERT + FAISS to Redwood-managed inference to improve latency & ops. Key scale: prod index ~22M documents (~180GB embeddings), current QPS spikes ~120 qps, typical qps 20-35. Primary concerns: quality regressions when migrating embedding model and introducing cross-encoder reranker, and cost per query at scale.

Requirements / targets: p95 tail latency <200ms end-to-end for single-query rerank flow; cost per active query (embedding + rerank) target <$0.004 at expected volume; strong audit logging and per-request data residency (US). Must support SSO/SAML and customer-managed KMS.

Technical notes: currently: offline SBERT-large embeddings, FAISS HNSW index, small on-prem GPU pool for reranker. Migration plan discussed: phased eval-driven rollout — run parallel embeddings (candidate vs baseline) on golden queries, compute NDCG / MRR / regression alarms via Redwood Evals harness. If embeddings candidate passes NDCG delta threshold (<0.7% drop) then enable cross-encoder reranker as canary (5% traffic) with automatic rollback conditions. SE recommended: index sampling strategy to mirror prod doc distribution (size, languages, domain-specific tokens).

Quotes & shorthand from calls: "We can't tolerate regressions in legal query quality"; "cost math looks off if we don't batch reranks"; "need clear rollback — don't want to wake up to lawyers complaining".

Operational asks: sample production slice for canary, replay pipeline for queries, monitoring hooks (per-route token/cost), alerting on eval regressions, run cost simulation for committed capacity vs pay-as-you-go.

Open items: final approval from security (KMS SLA + data residency proof), procurement sign-off on committed capacity, agreement on eval pass/fail thresholds and measurement queries.

Next immediate actions: spin up 5M slice canary index, run baseline vs embed-candidate NDCG sweep, schedule 2-week A/B with automated rollback conditions.
